angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 486,990 km at 50.94 pc = 0.13 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 19.6301 +/- 0.0197 mas (same row, RUWE 1.12): 50.94 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.7 solar radii from Hord et al. 2024, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-1683.01 in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024AJ....167..233H/abstract): 486,990 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.694661 solar masses from Hord et al. 2024, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-1683.01 in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024AJ....167..233H/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4402 K from Hord et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1683.01 in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024AJ....167..233H/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Hord et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1683.01 in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024AJ....167..233H/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-1683.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.590, rounded to two decimals
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-1683 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.78662, from TICv8 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....158..138S/abstract)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
